name: fig7-kinetic-parameters
title: Fig 7E-G — Kinetic parameters: growth depends sigmoidally on an enzyme's kcat (Vmax proxy)
question:
Does the reduced-but-genuine viva-Mgen cell reproduce Fig 7E-G's central
quantitative claim — that predicted growth rate depends on an enzyme's kinetic
parameter (kcat/Vmax), producing a SIGMOIDAL growth-vs-kcat curve that rises
from near-zero at low activity and saturates at the wild-type rate once the
enzyme is no longer rate-limiting?
hypothesis:
If a genuinely growth-limiting reaction's FBA flux bound is used as a kcat
proxy and swept over ~three decades (0.01–10x wild-type), growth_fraction
should rise monotonically with the bound and then plateau at 1.0, mirroring the
saturating kcat→growth dependence the paper uses to reconcile model and
experiment for lpdA/deoD/thyA.
objective:
Programmatically identify a growth-limiting reaction in the iPS189 network
(one whose bound binds when throttled yet whose growth recovers to the
wild-type plateau before the top of the sweep), sweep its flux bound over
np.logspace(-2, 1, 16) with MetabolismFbaReproductionProcess, and read out
whether the kcat→growth curve is monotonic, saturating, and has a clear
dynamic range.
description:
REDUCED / representative fidelity. kcat is modelled as a multiplicative scale
on a target reaction's FBA flux bound (a Vmax proxy) via
MetabolismFbaReproductionProcess(config={"reaction_bound_scale": {rid: s}}),
NOT explicit enzyme kinetics; the specific lpdA/deoD/thyA genetics are not
individually modelled. run.py first scans candidate reactions (central-carbon
shortlist plus every reaction carrying flux at the optimum) at scales
{0.05, 0.2, 1.0} and keeps those that are both limiting (growth drops when
throttled) and saturating (growth back at the wild-type plateau by 0.2x). The
chosen primary target is the leucine-uptake reaction EX_leu_DASH_L_e — an
amino-acid transporter Vmax proxy; M. genitalium is auxotrophic for most amino
acids, so amino-acid provisioning is a real growth-limiting kinetic step, the
same qualitative role the paper's biosynthetic enzymes play. Lysine uptake
(EX_lys_DASH_L_e) and potassium uptake (EX_k_e) are shown as secondary series.
Achieved (committed production run) for EX_leu_DASH_L_e: monotonic
(growth_is_monotonic_in_kcat = 1.0), saturating (growth_saturates = 1.0),
dynamic_range = 0.864 (growth 0.136 at 0.01x rising to 1.000 at >=0.1x).

simulation_set.name: baseline
simulation_set.condition: Canonical viva-Mgen fig7-kinetic-parameters run via sims/run.py (recorded in .pbg/runs.jsonl).

expected_behavior.name: growth-monotonic-in-kcat
expected_behavior.en: Growth rate increases monotonically with the enzyme's kcat proxy (Fig 7E).
expected_behavior.rationale: Relaxing a rate-limiting enzyme's Vmax can only help or leave growth unchanged, never hurt it — the kcat→growth curve is non-decreasing. Achieved 1.0 over the 16-point 0.01–10x sweep of EX_leu_DASH_L_e.

expected_behavior.name: growth-saturates-at-high-kcat
expected_behavior.en: Growth saturates at the wild-type rate once the enzyme is no longer rate-limiting (Fig 7E-G plateau).
expected_behavior.rationale: Beyond the kcat where the enzyme stops limiting flux, further increases give no extra growth — the curve plateaus. Growth at the top of the sweep is within 3% of the maximum. Achieved 1.0.

expected_behavior.name: kcat-has-dynamic-range
expected_behavior.en: Throttling the enzyme's kcat proxy moves growth appreciably (the reaction is genuinely limiting).
expected_behavior.rationale: A meaningful sigmoid requires the reaction to actually constrain growth when throttled; max minus min growth over the sweep must be clearly positive. Achieved 0.864.

behavior_tests.name: growth-monotonic-in-kcat
behavior_tests.description: Growth is non-decreasing across the increasing kcat-proxy sweep (flag == 1.0).

provenance.note: Relaxing a rate-limiting Vmax cannot decrease FBA growth; the kcat→growth curve is monotonic (Karr 2012 Fig 7E). Achieved 1.0.

behavior_tests.name: growth-saturates-at-high-kcat
behavior_tests.description: Growth at the top of the sweep is within 3% of the sweep maximum (flag == 1.0).

provenance.note: Past the point where the enzyme stops limiting flux, growth plateaus at the wild-type rate (Karr 2012 Fig 7E-G). Achieved 1.0.

behavior_tests.name: kcat-has-dynamic-range
behavior_tests.description: max minus min growth_fraction over the 0.01–10x sweep exceeds 0.3.

provenance.note: EX_leu_DASH_L_e is genuinely growth-limiting; sweeping its bound moves growth from 0.136 to 1.000. Achieved dynamic_range 0.864.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
The reduced cell reproduces Fig 7's qualitative kcat→growth law — a
monotonic, saturating sigmoid with a clear dynamic range — establishing that
tuning a rate-limiting enzyme's Vmax proxy moves predicted growth, the
mechanism the paper uses to reconcile model and experiment.

embed_visualizations.description: Growth fraction vs flux-bound scale (kcat/Vmax proxy, log x) for the leucine-uptake target and two secondary uptake reactions — a monotonic, saturating sigmoid (Fig 7E).

provenance.note: Karr et al. 2012, Fig 7E-G — predicted growth rate depends on an enzyme's kinetic parameter (kcat), producing a sigmoidal growth-vs-kcat curve; tuning kcat reconciles model and experiment for lpdA, deoD, thyA. Reproduced here at REDUCED fidelity with kcat as a multiplicative FBA flux-bound (Vmax) proxy on a growth-limiting reaction (EX_leu_DASH_L_e), not explicit enzyme kinetics.

conclusion:
The viva-Mgen cell reproduces Fig 7's central kcat→growth law at reduced
fidelity. Sweeping the growth-limiting leucine-uptake reaction
EX_leu_DASH_L_e's flux bound (a Vmax proxy) over 0.01–10x wild-type yields a
textbook sigmoid: growth_fraction rises monotonically from 0.136 at 0.01x,
crosses through the mid-range, and saturates at 1.000 by ~0.1x, giving a
dynamic range of 0.864. Both primary tests pass (monotonic = 1.0,
saturates = 1.0) and the reaction is genuinely limiting (dynamic_range 0.864 >
0.3) — matching the qualitative dependence the paper exploits to reconcile
model and experiment for lpdA/deoD/thyA. kcat is a flux-bound proxy, not
explicit enzyme kinetics, and the specific paper genetics are not individually
modelled.
